problem: Eliminate the crash window between mission mutation commit and durable request-result journal completion, then expose that guarantee on the worker runtime path.

candidates.name: unified-atomic-snapshot-runtime
candidates.notes: Mission mutation and request outcome share one lock/rename and a dedicated runtime composes authenticated request handling with the transactional store without rewriting the legacy queue path.

candidates.name: in-place-durable-queue-refactor
candidates.notes: Could make the legacy queue transactional directly, but touches mature lease/dependency code and expands regression scope before the new persistence contract is fully exercised.

candidates.name: two-store-reconciliation
candidates.notes: Smaller initial refactor, but ambiguous in-progress outcomes require action-specific inference and more recovery branches.

candidates.name: sqlite-or-external-transaction
candidates.notes: Best future scale/multi-Qube direction, but adds migration/deployment complexity before qrexec and secret lifecycle are validated.

why: It closes the LAB crash-consistency gap on a concrete worker runtime path with one persistence boundary and lower regression risk than rewriting the established DurableMissionQueue immediately. It preserves a clean migration path to SQLite or an external coordinator later.
failuresAndLessons: Separate atomic files are not a transaction: either file may commit before coordinator death.
A failed request record must be committed before surfacing the error; throwing inside the transaction callback rolled back the intended failed outcome and could permit unsafe retry semantics.
A narrow transactional runtime adapter gives stronger QA isolation than an immediate broad refactor of the legacy queue.
Atomic rename protects the visible snapshot, but full-file JSON rewrite is not the final high-throughput distributed design.
Registry heartbeat remains a separate state update; this is acceptable for LAB liveness but is not a cross-resource distributed transaction.
REAL-WORKER readiness still requires qrexec deployment/policy, secret lifecycle, worker requestId persistence, and multi-Qube crash/partition testing.
